t: Constraints Liberate, Liberties Constrain — Runar Bjarnason

q.x: > Constraints provide freedom. For a great video on this, see Runar Bjarnason's talk "Constraints Liberate, Liberties Constrain" ( [link] ).

desc:
As programmers, we tend to think of expressive power of a language or library as an unmitigated good. In this talk I want to show the contrary; that restraint and precision are usually better than power and flexibility. A constraint on component design leads to freedom and power when putting those components together into systems.

What’s more, this feature is built into the very nature of languag

recs.stt: Htmx and the Rule of Least Power
recs.x:
A compiler can reason about an AST far more easily than it can reason about a machine-code sequence, for instance. A compiler typically converts from AST to machine-code pretty late in the game, as you want to take advantage of the utility of the abstraction, not the unlimited power of directly working with instructions.
